Is Earnings Rebound Altering The Investment Case For Citigroup (C)?
Sasha Jovanovic
Mon, November 23, 2026 at 6:17 PM MST 4 min read
C
Trade C on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Citigroup has recently raised multiple tranches of fixed rate senior unsecured notes across maturities from 2028 to 2056, while also making leadership hires in equity capital markets and U.S. retail branches, and hosting a Taiwan Corporate Day that highlights its global services reach.

The mix of fresh bond funding, regional leadership changes, and deepening institutional engagement points to Citigroup focusing on balance sheet flexibility, capital markets execution and cross border client flows rather than headline trading activity.

We will look at how this combination of fresh bond issuance and executive reshaping fits into Citigroup's broader investment narrative.

Compare how Citigroup's funding and leadership reshuffle stacks up against other large financial institutions by scanning a curated set of list of solid balance sheet and fundamentals (23 results)

Citigroup Investment Narrative Recap

To own Citigroup, you need to believe the bank can keep turning its global Services, U.S. cards and wealth engines into steady returns while keeping risk under tight control. The analyst consensus Narrative on Simply Wall St expects services growth, AI driven efficiency and business simplification to support double digit returns on tangible equity. The latest bond funding and leadership moves look incremental rather than thesis changing for that view.

The most important near term swing factor remains execution on restructuring, capital return and the January Banamex and broader capital plans, while the biggest risk is still regulatory and conduct setbacks that could eat into those returns. Recent news does not materially change either the main catalyst or the key vulnerability.

The fresh run of fixed income offerings, including the US$30.325 million 6.05% notes due 2031 and US$59.367 million 6.00% notes due 2031, is the clearest operational link to the funding narrative. These senior unsecured, mostly callable issues extend Citigroup's maturity ladder and support the balance sheet that underpins the services led growth story.

For you as a shareholder, the relevance is practical rather than dramatic. Stable term funding helps Citigroup keep supporting cross border payments, securities services and U.S. cards while it pursues AI driven cost efficiencies and prepares for capital redeployment from Banamex. The risk side is that higher coupon debt raises interest expense, so execution on productivity and fee income needs to keep pace.

Citigroup's current narrative ties a forecast revenue level of US$108.8b and earnings of US$22.4b by 2029 to an assumed 9.3% yearly rise in revenue and an earnings increase of about US$4.5b from the US$17.9b earned today.

title: A $109 Billion Fund Just Bought These 3 Stocks

A $109 Billion Fund Just Bought These 3 Stocks

A $109 Billion Fund Just Bought These 3 Stocks ©@Omar_Nasif from pixabay via Canva, @Diego Maravilla © 2022 from Diego Maravilla via Canva
Key Takeaways

Harris Associates manages $109 billion. Its 13F filed Nov. 16 shows that Meta, Marsh and Citigroup were its biggest additions in the third quarter.

Meta and Citigroup have fallen since Sept. 30, and analysts' average targets sit well above both stocks.

Marsh's business is growing steadily, but its stock has climbed to within 2% of the Street's average target.

Of the three, Meta has the strongest case on the numbers, though heavy AI spending will keep its free cash flow negative in 2027.

Bill Nygren's Harris Associates, which runs the Oakmark funds, filed its 13F for the quarter ended Sept. 30 on Nov. 16. Its boldest move was in Meta Platforms (META:NASDAQ), where it grew its stake more than 500-fold to 2.43 million shares.

Its other two biggest additions were Marsh (MRSH:NYSE), up 24% to 10.78 million shares, and Citigroup (C:NYSE), up 30% to 11.34 million. Since the quarter ended, Meta is down 23% and Citi is down 15%, while Marsh is up 21%.

Meta is the big new bet

At Sept. 30, Harris's Meta shares were worth $1.76 billion. That's 2.3% of its 13F stocks and its No. 12 holding. It wasn't the only fund buying: Brad Gerstner's Altimeter added 25% to its Meta stake in the same quarter.

Meta's third-quarter revenue rose 26% to $64.6 billion, but capital spending of $34.9 billion outran the $32.8 billion of cash its operations brought in. On Oct. 21, a New Mexico court also ordered Meta to pay a $25 billion penalty, which Meta will appeal.

Analysts haven't budged. Their average price target is about where it was a year ago, $848 against $840:

Meta Platforms (META): analysts' consensus (mean) price target, $ per share, last year (TIKR)

That target is 51% above the stock, and even the lowest target, $650, is above it. At about 17x forward earnings, Meta trades well below its five-year average of 21.4x. Analysts expect $42.40 of normalized EPS for 2028, and the $848 target is 20x that. So the target needs no re-rating, only for the estimates to hold.

TIKR tracks 62 analysts on Meta Platforms. How many say "Buy"?

See the full breakdown of Buy, Hold, and Sell ratings on Meta Platforms, along with Wall Street's revenue and earnings estimates, all in one place. More than 500,000 investors use TIKR to research stocks like this one. See Meta Platforms' Analyst Ratings

Citi's returns are rising, and the stock got cheaper

Harris added 30% to Citi and ended the quarter with 11.34 million shares worth $1.47 billion, 1.9% of its 13F stocks. Citi's third-quarter GAAP net income rose 40% to $5.2 billion. Its return on tangible common equity was 12.6% for the first nine months, already inside the 11% to 13% it targets for 2027 and 2028. Management does expect fourth-quarter Markets revenue to fall about 20% from the third quarter, and its guidance implies a fourth-quarter return in the high single digits. Its next report is due Jan. 14.

title: UBS Set to Revise Capital Targets as Credit Suisse Integration Advances
detail:
UBS Set to Revise Capital Targets as Credit Suisse Integration Advances
Zacks Equity Research
Mon, November 23, 2026 at 10:16 AM MST 3 min read
UBS
UBS
WFC
C
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

UBS Group AG UBS plans to reassess its capital, profitability and shareholder return targets as the Credit Suisse integration advances. At the J.P. Morgan Financials Conference 2026 on Nov. 19, 2026, CFO Todd Tuckner indicated that the bank does not intend to maintain its common equity Tier 1 (CET1) capital ratio at the elevated level of 14% over the long term. Following the Credit Suisse acquisition, UBS Group raised its CET1 capital ratio target from 13% to approximately 14% to manage integration-related risks and additional capital requirements. As of Sept. 30, 2026, the ratio stood at 14.7%, with management expecting it to approach the 14% target by year-end 2026.

With integration nearing completion by year-end 2026, UBS Group plans to unveil revised financial targets alongside its fourth-quarter 2026 results in February 2027. The bank also intends to revisit its target of approximately 18% return on CET1 capital in 2028, while placing greater emphasis on return on tangible equity. Meanwhile, its cumulative gross cost savings reached $13.2 billion through the third quarter of 2026 and are expected to increase to approximately $13.7 billion by year-end, exceeding the previous target of $13.5 billion. These efficiencies, alongside the bank's targeted underlying cost-to-income ratio of below 70% on a 2026 exit-rate basis, are expected to support profitability and strengthen internal capital generation.

Improved capital efficiency and profitability could provide UBS with greater flexibility to enhance shareholder returns. The bank repurchased approximately $1.8 billion worth of shares in the third quarter of 2026 and expects to complete its $3-billion buyback program by the fourth quarter of 2026, ahead of its original target of the second quarter of 2027. Moreover, management continued accruing for mid-teens percentage dividend growth, underscoring its commitment to returning capital to shareholders.

However, proposed Swiss regulatory reforms remain a key challenge to UBS' capital planning and shareholder returns. Under existing and proposed measures, the bank could face cumulative incremental CET1 capital requirements of approximately $33 billion since the Credit Suisse acquisition, including additional capital obligations related to foreign subsidiaries. These requirements could offset integration-related savings, constrain funds available for dividends and buybacks, and limit the bank's ability to reduce capital buffers and revise its financial targets.

Overall, UBS' decision to revisit its capital and profitability targets reflects progress in integrating Credit Suisse and normalizing its capital position. Easing integration risks, substantial cost savings and improving operating efficiency could support stronger profitability and shareholder distributions. Nevertheless, uncertainty surrounding Swiss capital regulations remains a key challenge.

Citi slashed its Salesforce (NYSE:CRM) price target by nearly 25% on Monday, warning that sluggish demand for the software giant's core products could outweigh its artificial intelligence ambitions ahead of its upcoming earnings report.

CRM GF Value chart

Analyst Tyler Radke lowered his target to $198 from $263 while maintaining a Neutral rating, implying approximately 9.6% upside from Friday's closing price of $180.62.

The downgrade in expectations follows Citi's checks with Salesforce customers and partners, which suggest demand for traditional customer relationship management software remains weak.

The bank sees limited evidence that Salesforce's AI products can meaningfully accelerate companywide growth in the near term.

That raises questions about Agentforce, Salesforce's platform for deploying AI agents capable of handling customer service, sales and other business tasks.

Although AI remains central to CEO Marc Benioff's strategy, investors are increasingly focused on whether customer interest translates into substantial recurring revenue.

Salesforce shares have fallen approximately 20% in November, underperforming a broader rebound in software stocks earlier this month.

Investors Takeaway

Citi expects Salesforce to report fiscal third-quarter adjusted earnings of $3.38 per share on approximately $11.5 billion in revenue.

The upcoming report will test whether AI adoption is strengthening enough to offset slower growth in established software products.

Investors should watch subscription revenue, customer spending trends and management's commentary on Agentforce adoption.

The bigger question is whether Salesforce can convert its AI investments into faster growth before competitive pressures further weaken its core business.

Citigroup (NYSE:C) is moving its card business toward one type of customer, and its card chief explained why. Speaking at Citi's 15th Annual FinTech Conference on November 10, 2026, Pam Habner, Head of U.S. Consumer Cards, referenced industry data showing that general-purpose cardholders spend approximately nine times as much and borrow four times as much as private-label store card customers. She said Citi finds similar patterns in its own portfolio.

ymgerman / iStock Editorial via Getty Images
C Price Target — 24/7 Wall St.
Nine Times the Spend Points to Where Citi Is Headed

Habner put the U.S. credit card loan market at approximately $1.2 trillion. General-purpose cards make up roughly 85% of it and are expected to grow 5% to 6% annually. Private-label cards are expected to decline approximately 3% annually.

Citi's third-quarter results already show the shift. On the October 13, 2026 earnings call, CEO Jane Fraser said "our general-purpose portfolio drove 6% growth in total average loans." General-purpose spend volume rose 13% while private-label cards declined. Fraser added: "I think what we have been seeing is this shift to more of the co-brand proposition."

title: Wall Street Bulls Look Optimistic About Citigroup (C): Should You Buy?

Wall Street Bulls Look Optimistic About Citigroup (C): Should You Buy?
Zacks Equity Research
Mon, November 23, 2026 at 6:30 AM MST 4 min read
C
Trade C on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

When deciding whether to buy, sell, or hold a stock, investors often rely on analyst recommendations. Media reports about rating changes by these brokerage-firm-employed (or sell-side) analysts often influence a stock's price, but are they really important?

Before we discuss the reliability of brokerage recommendations and how to use them to your advantage, let's see what these Wall Street heavyweights think about Citigroup (C).

Citigroup currently has an average brokerage recommendation (ABR) of 1.65, on a scale of 1 to 5 (Strong Buy to Strong Sell), calculated based on the actual recommendations (Buy, Hold, Sell, etc.) made by 26 brokerage firms. An ABR of 1.65 approximates between Strong Buy and Buy.

Of the 26 recommendations that derive the current ABR, 16 are Strong Buy and three are Buy. Strong Buy and Buy respectively account for 61.5% and 11.5% of all recommendations.

Brokerage Recommendation Trends for C
Broker Rating Breakdown Chart for C

Check price target & stock forecast for Citigroup here>>>

While the ABR calls for buying Citigroup, it may not be wise to make an investment decision solely based on this information. Several studies have shown limited to no success of brokerage recommendations in guiding investors to pick stocks with the best price increase potential.

Do you wonder why? As a result of the vested interest of brokerage firms in a stock they cover, their analysts tend to rate it with a strong positive bias. According to our research, brokerage firms assign five "Strong Buy" recommendations for every "Strong Sell" recommendation.

This means that the interests of these institutions are not always aligned with those of retail investors, giving little insight into the direction of a stock's future price movement. It would therefore be best to use this information to validate your own analysis or a tool that has proven to be highly effective at predicting stock price movements.

Zacks Rank, our proprietary stock rating tool with an impressive externally audited track record, categorizes stocks into five groups, ranging from Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) to Zacks Rank #5 (Strong Sell), and is an effective indicator of a stock's price performance in the near future. Therefore, using the ABR to validate the Zacks Rank could be an efficient way of making a profitable investment decision.

ABR Should Not Be Confused With Zacks Rank

In spite of the fact that Zacks Rank and ABR both appear on a scale from 1 to 5, they are two completely different measures.

The ABR is calculated solely based on brokerage recommendations and is typically displayed with decimals (example: 1.28). In contrast, the Zacks Rank is a quantitative model allowing investors to harness the power of earnings estimate revisions. It is displayed in whole numbers -- 1 to 5.

2 Investment Bank Stocks to Buy as Industry Tailwinds Strengthen

While persistent inflation, elevated borrowing costs and the Federal Reserve's cautious monetary policy stance could temper dealmaking, the Zacks Investment Bank industry is expected to benefit from resilient economic growth and robust corporate investment, supporting mergers and acquisitions (M&As) and underwriting activities. Geopolitical tensions, trade uncertainties and market volatility are likely to sustain trading revenues and client engagement.

Rising investments in artificial intelligence (AI), technology and digital platforms may elevate near-term expenses but are expected to improve operational efficiency and long-term profitability. So, industry players like Citigroup, Inc. C and BGC Group, Inc. BGC are worth betting on.

Industry Description

The Zacks Investment Bank industry consists of firms that provide financial products and services, including advisory-based financial transactions to corporations, governments and financial institutions worldwide. These started as partnership firms focused on initial public offerings (IPOs), secondary equity offerings, brokerage and mergers and acquisitions (M&As). Gradually, the companies have evolved into providers of various other services, including securities research, proprietary trading and investment management. Industry players work mainly through three product segments: investment banking (M&As, advisory services and securities underwriting), asset management and trading and principal investments (proprietary and brokerage trading).

Themes Shaping the Future of the Investment Bank Industry

Underwriting and Advisory Businesses Momentum to Persist: Following a prolonged slowdown since 2022, investment banking activity has regained momentum, supported by the Trump administration's pro-business agenda, deregulation efforts and improving corporate confidence. Strategic restructuring, private equity transactions and consolidation are driving M&A activity, while favorable market conditions are supporting a selective IPO recovery. A resilient economy, AI-related investments and healthy transaction pipelines should support advisory and capital-markets revenues.

However, the recent U.S. midterm election results have introduced fresh policy uncertainty, with potential legislative gridlock and increased regulatory oversight that could affect dealmaking and underwriting activities. Additionally, geopolitical tensions, tariff uncertainties, elevated borrowing costs and cautious investor sentiment could delay deal execution and temper the pace of recovery. Despite these challenges, sustained corporate investment and financing requirements are expected to support investment banking revenue growth.

Trading Business to Remain Solid: Trading activity remains closely tied to macroeconomic developments, geopolitical tensions and market volatility. Since 2022, persistent economic uncertainty and geopolitical disruptions have sustained elevated trading volumes. The Trump administration's tariff policies, evolving monetary policy expectations, concerns over AI valuations and uncertainty following the recent U.S. midterm elections could prolong market volatility and delay normalization in trading activity.

Against this backdrop, investors are likely to continue repositioning portfolios in response to interest rate movements, policy shifts and geopolitical developments, supporting client engagement across asset classes. Increased demand for hedging and risk management solutions is also expected to further bolster trading desks. Hence, investment banks are expected to benefit from sustained trading activity, supporting solid trading revenues in the near term.

Technology to Improve Operating Efficiency: Investment banks are increasingly investing in AI, advanced trading platforms and automation to enhance client services and strengthen their competitive positions. Industry players are also focusing on attracting and retaining skilled professionals while upgrading technological infrastructure and developing innovative digital solutions. Although higher spending on technology, talent acquisition and platform modernization could elevate near-term operating expenses, these investments are expected to streamline operations, improve productivity and enhance long-term operating efficiency and profitability.
